title: China-to-Finland EV Charger Compliance Gap Matrix
provenance: AI-compiled, multi-model cross-checked, not human-verified. Informational only; confirm with the official regulator and a qualified professional. Not legal/certification/customs/market-access advice.

rows.target_requirement: EU public AC recharging points are subject to AFIR (Regulation (EU) 2023/1804) requirements for connector availability. AFIR Annex II specifies Type 2 for normal-power AC recharging points. IEC/EN 62196-2 describes the Type 2 technical connector design; the legal obligation is AFIR, while the IEC/EN standard is the technical specification route. Finland, as an EU member state, is directly subject to AFIR without transposition. Finnish winter conditions (down to -30°C or lower) require that Type 2 connectors and cables are rated and tested for cold-temperature operation, including cable flexibility at low temperature.
rows.china_equivalent: China uses GB/T 20234.2 for AC charging, which defines a physically distinct 7-pin connector incompatible with IEC Type 2. GB/T plugs cannot mate with EU Type 2 sockets.
rows.gap: Hardware connector is physically incompatible. A Chinese EV or EVSE designed only around a GB/T AC interface cannot interoperate with EU public Type 2 AC infrastructure without a physical inlet/socket and control-interface redesign. The connector body, pin count, and locking mechanism all differ. In Finland, cold-climate operation additionally requires verification that the Type 2 connector, cable, and locking mechanism function reliably at Finnish winter temperatures (down to -30°C or lower) — standard ambient test temperatures may not cover this range. Any adapter strategy for public infrastructure must be checked against AFIR and Finnish safety rules.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory legal obligation: AFIR requirements for publicly accessible AC recharging points, including Type 2 availability as specified in Annex II. IEC/EN 62196-2 is the voluntary technical connector standard/specification used to implement that legal requirement; it is not the legal obligation by itself.
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory in China for domestic market — GB/T 20234.2 required for EV sold in China

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Non-compliant for EU public charging interoperability as-is if the product only supports GB/T AC. EU public AC infrastructure must meet AFIR connector requirements, and IEC/EN 62196-2 Type 2 is the technical specification used for that route. GB/T AC interfaces are not a substitute for AFIR-compliant Type 2 compatibility. In Finland, additionally verify cold-climate connector and cable performance down to -30°C or lower.

rows.target_requirement: EU public DC recharging points are subject to AFIR (Regulation (EU) 2023/1804) requirements for connector availability. AFIR Annex II specifies Combo 2 for high-power DC recharging points. IEC/EN 62196-3 describes the CCS Combo 2 technical connector design; the legal obligation is AFIR, while the IEC/EN standard is the technical specification route. Finland applies AFIR directly. Cold-climate operation requirements are critical for Finnish installations: CCS2 connectors, cables, and locking mechanisms must function reliably at Finnish winter temperatures (down to -30°C or lower in northern Finland).
rows.china_equivalent: China uses GB/T 20234.3 for DC fast charging, defining a physically distinct 9-pin connector (CHAdeMO-influenced design) incompatible with CCS Combo 2. The pin layout, communication protocol (CAN vs. PLC), and inlet shape all differ.
rows.gap: Hardware connector is physically incompatible. Chinese EVs or EVSE with only a GB/T DC interface cannot fast-charge at EU CCS2 public stations without hardware and communication-stack redesign. The vehicle/charger communication stack (GB/T 27930 CAN vs. ISO 15118 / DIN 70121 PLC pathways in common EU CCS practice) also differs, compounding the incompatibility beyond the physical plug. For Finland, cold-climate performance is a critical additional requirement: CCS2 connectors and cables must be verified for reliable operation at Finnish winter temperatures (-30°C or below), and cold-start charging behaviour under low temperatures must be documented.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory legal obligation: AFIR requirements for publicly accessible high-power DC recharging points, including Combo 2 availability as specified in Annex II. IEC/EN 62196-3 is the voluntary technical connector standard/specification used to implement that legal requirement; it is not the legal obligation by itself.
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory in China for domestic market — GB/T 20234.3 required for DC fast-charge EV sold in China

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Non-compliant for EU public DC charging interoperability as-is if the product only supports GB/T DC. EU public DC infrastructure must meet AFIR connector requirements, and IEC/EN 62196-3 CCS Combo 2 is the technical specification used for that route. GB/T DC interfaces are not a substitute for AFIR-compliant Combo 2 compatibility. In Finland, additionally verify cold-climate connector, cable, and charging performance at -30°C or lower.

rows.requirement: Legal Mandate: AFIR vs. AFID and Transition Timeline
rows.target_requirement: Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 (AFIR) replaced Directive 2014/94/EU (AFID) with binding targets. AFIR entered into force 13 April 2024. New public charging pools must comply from that date; all existing pools must be upgraded to Type 2 / CCS2 by 2025–2026 depending on power level. AFIR is directly applicable in all EU member states without transposition, including Finland.
rows.china_equivalent: China's equivalent policy mandate is GB/T 20234 series (enforced via MIIT type-approval). No bilateral connector recognition or mutual acceptance agreement exists between China GB/T and EU IEC 62196 standards. (Confirmed: no bilateral connector or certification mutual recognition treaty between CN GB/T 20234 and EU IEC 62196 has been concluded as of June 2026.)
rows.gap: No harmonisation or mutual recognition between GB/T and IEC 62196 series. AFIR is a binding EU Regulation (not a Directive), meaning no member-state flexibility to accept GB/T connectors. Any EV destined for the Finnish/EU market must carry Type 2 (AC) and CCS Combo 2 (DC) inlets as a hard market-entry requirement.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory legal obligation: AFIR is directly applicable across EU member states including Finland from 13 April 2024 for in-scope publicly accessible recharging infrastructure. IEC/EN 62196 connector standards are technical specifications referenced/used to implement AFIR connector requirements, not standalone legal obligations.
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory domestically; no reciprocal obligation on EU side to accept GB/T

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Non-compliant as-is for EU public charging infrastructure where a product relies on Chinese GB/T connectors only. AFIR creates the binding EU obligation for in-scope public infrastructure; Type 2 / Combo 2 technical compatibility is the practical redesign item. This is a product and infrastructure interoperability gap, not merely a documentation gap. Finland applies AFIR directly as an EU member state.

rows.requirement: Fingrid / DSO Grid Connection — 230/400 V 50 Hz Finnish Network with Cold-Climate Requirements
rows.target_requirement: Finnish electricity supply is operated by distribution system operators (DSOs) at local level, with Fingrid managing the national transmission grid and Energiavirasto overseeing the electricity market. The low-voltage context is 230 V single-phase / 400 V three-phase at 50 Hz. That is the same frequency as China but a different nominal voltage from China's 220/380 V baseline. Grid-connected charger projects should be treated as site-specific electrical installations requiring DSO supply-capacity review, protection coordination, metering, earthing, harmonic and power-quality review, commissioning, and written project acceptance before energisation. Finnish conditions include extreme cold winters (down to -30°C or colder in northern Finland), which affect charger thermal ratings, enclosure heating, and cold-start performance requirements.
target_standards: Fingrid transmission grid connection requirements (for large installations)
Finnish DSO electricity network connection and project acceptance requirements
IEC 61000 series — electromagnetic compatibility and power quality
IEC 61851-1 — EV conductive charging system general requirements
rows.china_equivalent: China domestic charger installations are commonly documented under GB/T 18487.1-2023, GB/T 20234 connector standards, GB/T 27930-2023 for DC communication, and local grid-operator acceptance. China domestic supply is 220 V single-phase / 380 V three-phase at 50 Hz. The shared 50 Hz frequency does not mean voltage equivalence: Finland 230/400 V requires input-voltage, protection-threshold, thermal, and metering validation beyond the China baseline. China does not have cold-climate operating requirements comparable to Finnish winter conditions.
china_standards: China local grid operator project-acceptance requirements
rows.gap: Exporters must confirm that the charger covers 230 V single-phase / 400 V three-phase at 50 Hz, not only China's 220/380 V settings. Protection thresholds, leakage-current devices, metering accuracy, harmonic emissions, supply-capacity calculations, earthing, surge protection, and commissioning documents should be prepared for Finnish DSO review. Critical Finland-specific gap: cold-climate performance must be documented — minimum operating temperature (typically -30°C or lower for Finnish sites), enclosure heating system, anti-condensation measures, cold-start charging behaviour, and cable/connector flexibility at low temperature are all required. For outdoor Finnish installations, IP rating suitability for freeze-thaw cycling and snow/ice ingress should be verified.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory — grid-connected installations require Finnish DSO project review and acceptance; voltage is 230/400 V at 50 Hz, which differs from China 220/380 V despite the same frequency; cold-climate ratings are a practical mandatory requirement for Finnish outdoor installations
mandatory_status.cn: China grid-operator acceptance applies domestically and is not a Finnish DSO approval substitute; China 220/380 V evidence must be revalidated for Finland 230/400 V; no cold-climate equivalence

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Finland-ready EVSE needs Finnish DSO project acceptance and explicit 230/400 V 50 Hz validation. Do not describe the voltage as matching China: only the 50 Hz frequency matches, while nominal voltage differs from China's 220/380 V baseline. Cold-climate performance down to -30°C or lower is a critical Finland-specific requirement for outdoor installations that is absent from China domestic specifications.

rows.requirement: CE Conformity Assessment — LVD, EMC, RED (if wireless)
rows.target_requirement: EV chargers sold in Finland/EU must bear the CE marking, demonstrating conformity with all applicable EU legislation. Wired AC/DC chargers typically fall under LVD (2014/35/EU) and EMC Directive (2014/30/EU); chargers with wireless communication (e.g., Wi-Fi, Bluetooth for smart charging) additionally require conformity with RED (2014/53/EU). Conformity is generally established by manufacturer self-declaration supported by a technical file. Harmonised EN standards are voluntary routes to presumption of conformity, not mandatory legal requirements in themselves. In Finland, Tukes is the market surveillance authority for LVD and EMC compliance.
target_standards: EN IEC 61851-21-2 (EMC for off-board EV chargers)
rows.china_equivalent: In China, EV chargers require China Compulsory Certification (CCC) under the GB/T and GB standards regime. Key standards include GB/T 18487.1 (AC charging system) and GB/T 20234 series (connectors). CCC is a mandatory third-party certification through designated bodies (CABs); it does not involve self-declaration and is structurally different from CE's conformity-based model.
rows.gap: Chinese manufacturers must obtain CE marking via EU-recognised conformity assessment routes (self-declaration under harmonised EN standards or notified-body involvement for certain RED equipment). CCC certification is not recognised in the EU and does not substitute for CE. Manufacturers must generate EU-specific technical documentation, test reports referencing EN standards, and an EU Declaration of Conformity — none of which are produced as part of the CCC process. Finnish Tukes conducts market surveillance and can require product withdrawal for non-compliant CE-marked products.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory legal obligation: CE marking and conformity with all applicable EU directives/regulations before EU/Finnish market access. Harmonised EN standards are voluntary presumption-of-conformity tools; alternatives are allowed if compliance is demonstrated. Tukes enforces in Finland.

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] CE marking is mandatory before placing EV chargers on the Finnish/EU market. CCC does not substitute for CE. Manufacturers must independently build EU technical files and, for wireless-enabled chargers, ensure RED compliance where applicable. Harmonised EN standards may support presumption of conformity but are not the mandatory legal obligation themselves. Tukes is the Finnish market surveillance authority.

rows.requirement: EU Declaration of Conformity (DoC) and Technical File
rows.target_requirement: Before placing a product on the Finnish/EU market, the manufacturer (or its EU authorised representative) must draw up an EU Declaration of Conformity (DoC) listing all applicable directives and the harmonised standards applied, and must compile and retain a technical file for at least 10 years. The DoC must be made available to market surveillance authorities on request. Requirements are set out in each applicable directive (LVD Art. 15, EMCD Art. 14, RED Art. 19) and in Decision 768/2008/EC (modular conformity assessment). Tukes can request the DoC and technical file as part of Finnish market surveillance.
rows.china_equivalent: Under the Chinese CCC regime, the equivalent documentary output is the CCC certificate issued by the designated certification body, accompanied by type-test reports. There is no manufacturer self-declaration equivalent to the EU DoC; the certificate is issued by a third party. Post-certificate, manufacturers must maintain a production consistency system audited periodically by the CAB.
china_standards: CNCA-C25-01:2024 (CCC implementation rules for EV charging equipment — effective 1 March 2025, supersedes any prior voluntary-only scheme; issued CNCA Announcement No. 25/2024)
Measures for the Administration of Compulsory Product Certification (SAMR 2020)
rows.gap: Chinese manufacturers exporting to Finland must create an EU-format DoC from scratch — listing each applicable EU directive, the specific harmonised standards applied, the manufacturer's name and address (or EU authorised representative's), and a traceable signatory. The CCC certificate neither replaces nor simplifies this; test data generated for CCC may be re-used only if it was produced against equivalent EN test methods, which requires engineering review.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory — must accompany product or be available on request; Tukes enforces in Finland
mandatory_status.cn: N/A — replaced by third-party CCC certificate regime

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] An EU DoC is a legal document that manufacturers or their EU representatives must sign and retain. It cannot be delegated to a test lab or certification body. Chinese exporters with only CCC documentation must draft the DoC in-house or engage an EU-based compliance consultant. Tukes in Finland can request the DoC and technical file during market surveillance.

rows.requirement: EU Economic Operator / Authorised Representative — Regulation (EU) 2019/1020
rows.target_requirement: Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 on market surveillance and product compliance requires that products placed on the EU market have an identifiable 'responsible economic operator' established in the EU. For products manufactured outside the EU, this means the importer or, if no EU importer, a mandated EU authorised representative (Art. 4). The responsible operator must: hold the DoC and technical file or ensure they are accessible; register in RAPEX/ICSMS where required; cooperate with market surveillance authorities; and take corrective action if a product is non-compliant. This obligation applies to EV chargers as CE-marked electrical equipment. In Finland, Tukes is the market surveillance authority that cooperates with the EU network.
rows.china_equivalent: China has no direct regulatory equivalent requiring a domestic responsible operator for export-bound products. Chinese manufacturers exporting abroad appoint foreign distributors or agents commercially, but there is no statutory requirement to designate an EU-resident legal representative responsible for CE compliance and market surveillance cooperation.
rows.gap: This is a structural gap with no Chinese regulatory analogue. A Chinese EV charger manufacturer shipping directly to Finnish customers (e.g., via e-commerce) must appoint an EU-established authorised representative before the first unit enters the EU market. Without one, the product cannot legally be placed on the EU market under Regulation 2019/1020. The AR must be named on the product label or documentation.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for non-EU manufacturers without an EU importer

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Chinese manufacturers without an EU importer must appoint an EU-established authorised representative. This is a hard legal gate under Regulation 2019/1020 — no EU AR means the product cannot lawfully enter the EU market, regardless of CE marking status. Tukes in Finland cooperates with the EU market surveillance network.

rows.requirement: AFIR — Public EV Charging: Ad-hoc Payment, Interoperability and Technical Specifications (Finland National Action Plan)
rows.target_requirement: Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 (AFIR) mandates functional requirements for publicly accessible EV recharging points in all EU member states including Finland. AFIR-confirmed requirements include: (1) ad-hoc charging without a subscription or contract, with the payment instruments required by AFIR for relevant publicly accessible recharging points; (2) transparent price information before a charging session starts; (3) digital connectivity, smart recharging capability, static data and dynamic data obligations for publicly accessible infrastructure; (4) AFIR Annex II technical specifications for publicly accessible recharging points, including Type 2 for normal-power AC recharging points and Combo 2 for high-power DC recharging points; and (5) TEN-T deployment targets for recharging pools. Finland has an established national EV policy and alternative fuels infrastructure plan; verify current Finnish NAP implementation status via Energiavirasto for the latest national deployment targets.
target_standards: AFIR Annex II (technical specifications for publicly accessible recharging points)
Finnish National Action Plan for Alternative Fuels Infrastructure — verify current status via Energiavirasto (energiavirasto.fi)
rows.china_equivalent: China has no direct regulatory equivalent to AFIR's functional public-charging requirements. The closest standards are GB/T 34658 (interoperability requirements) and NB/T 33025 (communication protocols for EV charging), plus GB/T 27930 (DC charging communication). Chinese public chargers are increasingly connected via operator platforms (e.g., State Grid, Southern Grid, TELD), but AFIR-equivalent ad-hoc payment, data-access, smart recharging and EU connector requirements are not mandated by Chinese regulation.
china_standards: NB/T 33025-2016 (EV DC charging communication protocol — EVSE side)
GB/T 27930-2015 (communication protocol between off-board charger and BMS)
rows.gap: Significant functional gap for public charging deployments in Finland: (1) ad-hoc payment functionality may need to be added for EU public deployments; (2) digital connectivity, smart recharging, data-access and roaming/data exchange obligations may differ from proprietary Chinese operator platforms; (3) AFIR Annex II connector specifications differ from Chinese GB/T connector practice; (4) Finland's cold climate introduces additional hardware requirements for outdoor public chargers that must be addressed alongside AFIR functional requirements. These AFIR requirements apply primarily to charge point operators (CPOs), but hardware and software capability must be available at installation.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for publicly accessible recharging points in Finland/EU under Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 (AFIR); Finnish NAP sets national deployment obligations — verify current status via Energiavirasto.
mandatory_status.cn: Not mandated — AFIR-equivalent ad-hoc payment, data-access, smart recharging and EU connector requirements are absent from Chinese public charging regulations.

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] AFIR introduces functional requirements for publicly accessible charging points in Finland, including ad-hoc payment, price transparency, digital connectivity, smart recharging, data obligations and Annex II connector specifications. Chinese charger hardware intended for Finnish public deployment must be verified for AFIR compliance and cold-climate performance before installation.

rows.requirement: OCPP, EMC, Radio Modules, and Power Quality
rows.target_requirement: Networked EV chargers in Finland should be specified for OCPP back-office interoperability where a charge-point operator, fleet operator, public-sector project, or DSO-linked programme requires remote monitoring, billing, diagnostics, or load management. Electrical and electronic emissions and immunity evidence should align with IEC 61000 EMC and power-quality standards. Cellular, Wi-Fi, RFID, payment, or smart-metering modules may trigger additional communications, spectrum, cybersecurity, and data-interface checks under Finnish project or national requirements. In Finland, Traficom (Finnish Transport and Communications Agency) regulates radio spectrum and type approvals for radio equipment; relevant CE marking under RED (2014/53/EU) is required for equipment with radio modules.
target_standards: OCPP — Open Charge Point Protocol for networked EV chargers
IEC 61000 series — electromagnetic compatibility and power quality
IEC 61851-24 — digital communication between DC EV charging station and EV
Directive 2014/53/EU (RED) — for radio-module-equipped chargers requiring CE marking
Traficom (Finnish Transport and Communications Agency) radio spectrum and type-approval requirements for radio modules where in scope
rows.china_equivalent: China DC fast chargers commonly use GB/T 27930-2023 CAN communication between the off-board charger and vehicle BMS. This is not OCPP back-office communication and is not the CCS2 communication direction. China-market chargers may also include China-specific payment, SIM, cloud, and operator integrations that need reconfiguration for Finnish operators, roaming, language (Finnish/Swedish/English), currency (EUR), and data interfaces.
china_standards: China radio module approvals where applicable
rows.gap: Exporters must confirm the OCPP version, charge-point-management-system integration, remote diagnostics, load management, payment or RFID flow, SIM or communications module approval path, and IEC 61000 EMC reports for the final Finland configuration. For DC CCS2 products, GB/T 27930 must not be presented as the relevant communication evidence. Harmonic current and immunity data should be reviewed against the specific Finnish DSO supply point requirements. For Finland, additional checks include: (1) Finnish/Swedish/English language interface for user-facing displays and documentation; (2) cold-climate-rated SIM modules and communication hardware (operating temperatures down to -30°C or lower); (3) Traficom radio module type approval where RED applies.

mandatory_status.target: Project-specific but commonly mandatory for networked public, fleet, or utility-linked chargers in Finland; EMC and power-quality evidence is expected where required by Fingrid, DSO, Traficom, tender, or site-owner specifications; RED CE marking mandatory for radio-equipped chargers
mandatory_status.cn: GB/T 27930 is China domestic DC vehicle-charger communication and is not OCPP or CCS2 back-office evidence

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Finnish networked chargers should be validated for OCPP integration, IEC 61000 EMC and power quality, Traficom radio module requirements, and local communications requirements. GB/T 27930 alone does not satisfy OCPP, CCS2 communication, or back-office interoperability needs. Finnish/Swedish/English language interfaces and cold-climate-rated communication hardware (-30°C or lower) are Finland-specific requirements.

rows.requirement: Low Voltage Safety — EV Charging Equipment (General)
rows.target_requirement: EV charging equipment placed on the Finnish/EU market must comply with the Low Voltage Directive 2014/35/EU, ensuring it is designed and manufactured to be safe when correctly installed and maintained. Equipment must meet the Essential Safety Requirements (Annex I) covering protection against electric shock, insulation, overcurrent/overtemperature protection, and clearances. Harmonised standard EN IEC 61851-1:2019 (Mode 1–4 conductive charging, AC and DC, general requirements) provides a presumption of conformity. In Finland, Tukes (Finnish Safety and Chemicals Agency) is the LVD market surveillance authority.
target_standards: EN IEC 61851-1:2019 — Electric vehicle conductive charging system — Part 1: General requirements
rows.china_equivalent: China commonly references GB/T 18487.1-2015 (Electric vehicle conductive charging system — General requirements), which is technically aligned with IEC 61851-1 but incorporates national deviations. It is enforced under the GB framework administered by SAMR/SAC. GB/T 18487.1 testing and certification by a Chinese CNAS-accredited lab is NOT recognised as equivalent to EN IEC 61851-1 testing under the EU LVD conformity assessment pathway.
china_standards: GB/T 18487.1-2015 — Electric vehicle conductive charging system — General requirements (SAMR/SAC)
rows.gap: Exporters should build an EU conformity file against the LVD essential safety requirements and may use EN IEC 61851-1:2019 testing as evidence for presumption of conformity. Existing Chinese GB/T 18487.1 test reports do not automatically substitute because scope, deviations, connector assumptions and documentation differ. A Notified Body is not mandatory for LVD; manufacturer self-declaration with a Technical File is the normal route. Documentation gap: EU Declaration of Conformity, CE marking, and EU-language (Finnish/Swedish/English) technical instructions are all required. Finland-specific: cold-climate (-30°C or lower) operating range must be declared and verified for outdoor chargers.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory legal obligation: Directive 2014/35/EU and CE marking before EU/Finnish market placement. EN IEC 61851-1:2019 is voluntary harmonised-standard evidence for presumption of conformity; alternative technical solutions are allowed if the manufacturer demonstrates compliance with the LVD essential safety requirements. Tukes enforces in Finland.
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory for domestic market — GB/T 18487.1 compliance required under SAMR framework

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] CE marking under LVD 2014/35/EU is mandatory. EN IEC 61851-1:2019 is a voluntary harmonised standard that can grant presumption of conformity for general EV conductive charging; it is not the legal obligation itself. Chinese GB/T 18487.1 certification does not by itself satisfy the EU conformity assessment pathway; EU evidence against the LVD requirements is needed. Tukes is the Finnish market surveillance authority. Finnish-language or Swedish-language instructions may be required.

rows.requirement: DC Charging Station Safety — EV Conductive Charging
rows.target_requirement: DC charging stations (Mode 4, off-board chargers) placed on the Finnish/EU market must comply with the Low Voltage Directive 2014/35/EU where within scope. EN IEC 61851-23:2023 (Electric vehicle conductive charging system — Part 23: DC EV charging station) is a current product standard that may be used as technical evidence and, where cited as harmonised, gives presumption of conformity; it is not itself the mandatory legal obligation. Key technical topics include isolation monitoring, interlock systems, control pilot functions, maximum voltage/current ratings, and communication protocols for DC supply. For Finland, outdoor DC charging stations must be rated and verified for cold-climate operation down to at least -30°C (lower in northern Finland), with particular attention to enclosure heating, cold-start protocols, and condensation prevention.
target_standards: EN IEC 61851-23:2023 — Electric vehicle conductive charging system — Part 23: DC EV charging station (current edition, supersedes 2014)
rows.china_equivalent: China's DC charging station domestic equivalent is GB/T 18487.3-2001 (AC/DC electric vehicle charging station — the only published Part 3 of the 18487 series; note: a GB/T 18487.3-2015 does not exist). The current DC system standard is GB/T 18487.5-2024 (DC charging system for GB/T 20234.3 connector). The DC coupler standard is GB/T 20234.3-2023 (superseded by GB/T 20234.3-2023 which supports up to 1500 V / 800 A). CQC or CNAS certification to these Chinese standards is not accepted under the EU LVD CE marking pathway.
china_standards: GB/T 18487.3-2001 — Electric vehicle conductive charging system — AC/DC electric vehicle charging station (only published edition; no 2015 revision exists)
GB/T 18487.5-2024 — Electric vehicle conductive charging system — Part 5: DC charging system for GB/T 20234.3 (current DC system standard)
GB/T 20234.3-2023 — Connection set for conductive charging of electric vehicles — Part 3: DC charging coupler (supersedes 2015 edition)
rows.gap: DC charging stations exported to Finland should be assessed against the LVD essential safety requirements and may use EN IEC 61851-23:2023 testing as presumption-of-conformity evidence where applicable. Particular attention is needed for: (1) CCS2 (Combined Charging System Type 2) connector compliance vs. Chinese GB/T connector; (2) isolation monitoring requirements per European grid topology; (3) CHAdeMO or CCS2 communication protocol compatibility; (4) Finland-specific: cold-climate operation rating to at least -30°C for outdoor Finnish installations, including enclosure heater sizing, cold-start DC output behaviour, and freeze-thaw seal integrity.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory legal obligation: CE marking under Directive 2014/35/EU where the charger is within LVD scope. EN IEC 61851-23:2023 is a voluntary technical standard that may support presumption of conformity where harmonised/cited; alternatives are allowed if the manufacturer demonstrates compliance with the Directive. Tukes enforces in Finland.
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory — GB/T 18487.5-2024 is the current DC charging system standard; CCC mandatory from 1 March 2025 under CNCA-C25-01:2024

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] DC charging stations require CE marking under the applicable EU legislation, including LVD where in scope. EN IEC 61851-23:2023 is a voluntary product standard used as technical evidence or presumption-of-conformity support where harmonised; it is not mandatory in itself. Chinese GB/T 18487.3 certification is not accepted as an EU conformity assessment substitute. A significant hardware gap exists where Chinese DC stations use GB/T connectors incompatible with EU CCS2 practice. Finland-specific: cold-climate rating to -30°C or lower is critical for outdoor Finnish installations.

rows.requirement: Electrical Installation Safety — EV Charging in Buildings (IEC 60364-7-722) with Cold-Climate Considerations
rows.target_requirement: EU member-state electrical installation law and grid/installer rules govern the building-side circuits supplying EV charging points. IEC 60364-7-722 / HD 60364-7-722 provide the commonly adopted technical installation route covering protective measures (RCD type B or A+DC detection), wiring, earthing, and load management. These standards apply to the building-side installation infrastructure, not the charger product itself, but exported EV chargers should be compatible with these installation requirements so they can be accepted by Finnish installers and DSOs. In Finland, SFS adopts IEC/CENELEC standards and Finnish building regulations (Maankäyttö- ja rakennusasetus) incorporate the relevant IEC installation requirements. Additionally, Finnish outdoor installations must address cold-climate wiring requirements, cable flexibility at low temperatures, and earthing system performance in permafrost or frost-heave conditions in northern Finland.
target_standards: IEC 60364-7-722:2018 — Low-voltage electrical installations — Part 7-722: Requirements for special installations or locations — Supply of electric vehicles

HD 60364-7-722 (CENELEC harmonised document, adopted by EU member states) (confirmed: HD 60364-7-722:2018 is the current CENELEC harmonisation document, approved 27 August 2018; adopted in Finland as SFS-HD 60364-7-722)
Finnish building regulations (Maankäyttö- ja rakennusasetus) incorporating IEC installation requirements
rows.china_equivalent: China addresses EV charging installation primarily through GB 50966-2014 (Code for design of electric vehicle charging station) and GB/T 51313-2018 (Technical standard for electric vehicle charging infrastructure), administered by the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development (MOHURD). These cover site design and installation but differ from IEC 60364-7-722 in RCD type requirements, earthing system assumptions (TN-S vs. Chinese practice), and load management protocols. Chinese installation documentation is not accepted as evidence of compliance with Finnish/EU member-state installation standards. China does not have specific cold-climate installation requirements comparable to Finnish conditions.
china_standards: GB 50966-2014 — Code for design of electric vehicle charging station (MOHURD) (confirmed to exist; enforced by MOHURD/MIIT)
GB/T 51313-2018 — Technical standard for electric vehicle charging infrastructure (confirmed to exist; enforced by MOHURD/MIIT)
rows.gap: IEC 60364-7-722 / HD 60364-7-722 are installation standards — they govern fixed wiring and protection devices at the building side, not the charger product itself. However, exported EV chargers should declare compatibility with Type B RCDs or incorporate internal DC fault protection to allow Type A RCDs under EU installation practice. A charger that requires installation conditions not achievable under Finnish/EU electrical codes will fail field acceptance. Chinese charger datasheets often omit compatibility statements expected by Finnish installers. Finland-specific installation gaps: (1) cold-climate cable selection (rated for -40°C or colder for outdoor Finnish routes); (2) earthing system continuity in permafrost or frost-heave conditions in northern Finland; (3) SFS-adopted installation standards may impose additional requirements beyond the base HD 60364-7-722.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory legal obligation sits in Finnish/EU member-state electrical installation law and grid codes. IEC 60364-7-722 / HD 60364-7-722 / SFS-adopted equivalents are voluntary or nationally adopted technical standards commonly used to demonstrate accepted installation practice; product compatibility is a practical market requirement. Finnish cold-climate installation requirements are a practical mandatory requirement for outdoor chargers.
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory for domestic installation — GB 50966 / GB/T 51313 under MOHURD; no cold-climate equivalence for Finnish conditions

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] IEC 60364-7-722 / HD 60364-7-722 govern building-side installation practice as adopted through Finnish national rules (SFS). EV chargers exported to Finland should be compatible with the RCD and earthing requirements expected by Finnish installers and DSOs. This is distinct from product-level CE marking under LVD, but non-compatibility can block field installation. Chinese installation standards (GB 50966 / GB/T 51313) are not substitutes. Finland's extreme cold winters impose additional cold-climate cable, earthing, and installation requirements not present in Chinese domestic practice.
